questions.question: What is the primary role of a Ludwig configuration?
options: It replaces the need for held-out evaluation
It declares feature, model, preprocessing, and training choices that Ludwig turns into an executable pipeline
It guarantees that every input field exists at serving time
It stores all production requests inside the model artifact
questions.explanation: The configuration is an executable ML contract. Ludwig builds the pipeline from it, but the team still owns data validity, evaluation design, release policy, and operations.

questions.question: Why is resolution_code an unsafe input when predicting a ticket's destination queue?
options: Category features cannot be used by Ludwig
It is too short to encode
It is recorded after the ticket workflow and can leak information about the outcome
It requires a random split
questions.explanation: A post-outcome field gives training examples information that is unavailable at decision time. Held-out scores can look strong while the deployed model fails.

questions.question: The same customer opens many similar tickets. Which evaluation design best limits entity leakage?
options: Randomly place individual rows into train, validation, and test sets
Use all rows for training and report training accuracy
Create a fixed split column that keeps each customer in one partition
Increase the number of epochs
questions.explanation: A group-aware partition prevents near-duplicate customer history from appearing on both sides of the evaluation boundary. Ludwig can consume the upstream split through a fixed split column.

questions.question: What does the output_features section declare?
options: The values the model must predict and their feature types
Only the HTTP response status codes
The machines used for distributed training
The fields that must be removed from the training set
questions.explanation: Output features name the prediction targets and their types. Their decoders, losses, and metrics follow from or refine that contract.

questions.question: Why should a team evaluate the saved model artifact again on a held-out dataset?
options: To make the YAML file shorter
To verify the artifact and decision metrics on data that did not train the model
To avoid versioning preprocessing metadata
To replace request-schema tests
questions.explanation: Artifact-level evaluation checks the model that will actually be released. The held-out set must contain ground-truth output columns so metrics can be computed.

questions.question: A serving container has new weights but preprocessing metadata from the previous run. What is the safe response?
options: Release all traffic because the weights are current
Increase the HTTP timeout
Block or roll back and rebuild one coherent artifact bundle
Ignore the mismatch if offline accuracy was high
questions.explanation: Feature metadata determines how values become tensors. Mixing it with different weights breaks training-serving parity and invalidates the evidence used to approve the candidate.

questions.question: Unknown production categories increase sharply, but requests still match the schema. What is the most informative bounded action?
options: Shadow the candidate and measure category and prediction behavior before it affects decisions
Delete the unknown values from logs
Train on the production requests without labels immediately
Promote the model to all traffic
questions.explanation: Shadowing collects representative live evidence without making the uncertain candidate authoritative. The team can then decide whether preprocessing, data, or retraining must change.

questions.question: Which responsibility remains with the engineering team when using Ludwig?
options: None; declarative training guarantees production readiness
Only writing neural-network layers by hand
Choosing valid data, metrics, release gates, security controls, and operational ownership
Only selecting the color of training charts
questions.explanation: Ludwig reduces custom model-pipeline code. It does not choose the business objective, detect every leakage path, define acceptable errors, or operate a reliable production service.
